inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court granted regular bail to a man accused under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, ruling that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a contact in Pakistan is not enough to justify keeping him locked up. He was allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based "Punjabi Kuri." This decision stands as a necessary check against the misuse of security laws that disproportionately harm individuals and reinforce systemic inequality by prioritizing vague threats over due process and civil liberties. The notion that courts are somehow weakening the nation by protecting the rights of the accused is just a familiar excuse to preserve power structures that have long ignored the vulnerabilities of those caught in these systems.
